paragraphs.text: After these things there was a feast of the Jews; and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦν ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta ēn heortē tōn Ioudaiōn, kai anebē Iēsous eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: Now there is in Jerusalem by the sheep [gate] a pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porches.
paragraphs.original: ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ Βηθεσδά, πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα·
paragraphs.translit: estin de en tois Hierosolymois epi tē probatikē kolymbēthra hē epilegomenē Hebraisti Bēthesda, pente stoas echousa·

paragraphs.text: In these lay a multitude of them that were sick, blind, halt, withered, [waiting for the moving of the water.]
paragraphs.original: ἐν ταύταις κατέκειτο πλῆθος τῶν ἀσθενούντων, τυφλῶν, χωλῶν, ξηρῶν.
paragraphs.translit: en tautais katekeito plēthos tōn asthenountōn, typhlōn, chōlōn, xērōn.

paragraphs.text: [for an angel of the Lord went down at certain seasons into the pool, and troubled the water: whosoever then first after the troubling of the waters stepped in was made whole, with whatsoever disease he was holden.]
And a certain man was there, who had been thirty and eight years in his infirmity.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δέ τις ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ τριάκοντα ὀκτὼ ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ēn de tis anthrōpos ekei triakonta oktō etē echōn en tē astheneia autou·

paragraphs.text: When Jesus saw him lying, and knew that he had been now a long time [in that case], he saith unto him, Wouldest thou be made whole?
paragraphs.original: τοῦτον ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς κατακείμενον, καὶ γνοὺς ὅτι πολὺν ἤδη χρόνον ἔχει, λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλεις ὑγιὴς γενέσθαι;
paragraphs.translit: touton idōn ho Iēsous katakeimenon, kai gnous hoti polyn ēdē chronon echei, legei autō· Theleis hygiēs genesthai;

paragraphs.text: The sick man answered him, Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool: but while I am coming, another steppeth down before me.
paragraphs.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ ἀσθενῶν· Κύριε, ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἔχω ἵνα ὅταν ταραχθῇ τὸ ὕδωρ βάλῃ με εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν· ἐν ᾧ δὲ ἔρχομαι ἐγὼ ἄλλος πρὸ ἐμοῦ καταβαίνει.
paragraphs.translit: apekrithē autō ho asthenōn· Kyrie, anthrōpon ouk echō hina hotan tarachthē to hydōr balē me eis tēn kolymbēthran· en hō de erchomai egō allos pro emou katabainei.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto him, Arise, take up thy bed, and walk.
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.
paragraphs.translit: legei autō ho Iēsous· Egeire aron ton krabatton sou kai peripatei.

paragraphs.text: And straightway the man was made whole, and took up his bed and walked. Now it was the sabbath on that day.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο ὑγιὴς ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἦρε τὸν κράβαττον αὐτοῦ καὶ περιεπάτει. Ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eutheōs egeneto hygiēs ho anthrōpos kai ēre ton krabatton autou kai periepatei. Ēn de sabbaton en ekeinē tē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: So the Jews said unto him that was cured, It is the sabbath, and it is not lawful for thee to take up thy bed.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ τεθεραπευμένῳ· Σάββατόν ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἆραι τὸν κράβαττον.
paragraphs.translit: elegon oun hoi Ioudaioi tō tetherapeumenō· Sabbaton estin, kai ouk exestin soi arai ton krabatton.

paragraphs.text: But he answered them, He that made me whole, the same said unto me, Take up thy bed, and walk.
paragraphs.original: ὃς δὲ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ποιήσας με ὑγιῆ ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.
paragraphs.translit: hos de apekrithē autois· Ho poiēsas me hygiē ekeinos moi eipen Aron ton krabatton sou kai peripatei.

paragraphs.text: They asked him, Who is the man that said unto thee, Take up [thy bed], and walk?
paragraphs.original: ἠρώτησαν οὖν αὐτόν· Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ εἰπών σοι· Ἆρον καὶ περιπάτει;
paragraphs.translit: ērōtēsan oun auton· Tis estin ho anthrōpos ho eipōn soi· Aron kai peripatei;

paragraphs.text: But he that was healed knew not who it was; for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in the place.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἰαθεὶς οὐκ ᾔδει τίς ἐστιν, ὁ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐξένευσεν ὄχλου ὄντος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de iatheis ouk ēdei tis estin, ho gar Iēsous exeneusen ochlou ontos en tō topō.

paragraphs.text: Afterward Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing befall thee.
paragraphs.original: μετὰ ταῦτα εὑρίσκει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἴδε ὑγιὴς γέγονας· μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε, ἵνα μὴ χεῖρόν σοί τι γένηται.
paragraphs.translit: meta tauta heuriskei auton ho Iēsous en tō hierō kai eipen autō· Ide hygiēs gegonas· mēketi hamartane, hina mē cheiron soi ti genētai.

paragraphs.text: The man went away, and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him whole.
paragraphs.original: ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀνήγγειλεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὸν ὑγιῆ.
paragraphs.translit: apēlthen ho anthrōpos kai anēngeilen tois Ioudaiois hoti Iēsous estin ho poiēsas auton hygiē.

paragraphs.text: And for this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the sabbath.
paragraphs.original: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐδίωκον οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι ταῦτα ἐποίει ἐν σαββάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai dia touto ediōkon hoi Ioudaioi ton Iēsoun hoti tauta epoiei en sabbatō.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh even until now, and I work.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς· Ὁ πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apekrinato autois· Ho patēr mou heōs arti ergazetai kagō ergazomai.

paragraphs.text: For this cause therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only brake the sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο οὖν μᾶλλον ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι ὅτι οὐ μόνον ἔλυε τὸ σάββατον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πατέρα ἴδιον ἔλεγε τὸν θεόν, ἴσον ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν τῷ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto oun mallon ezētoun auton hoi Ioudaioi apokteinai hoti ou monon elye to sabbaton, alla kai patera idion elege ton theon, ison heauton poiōn tō theō.

paragraphs.text: Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father doing: for what things soever he doeth, these the Son also doeth in like manner.
paragraphs.original: Ἀπεκρίνατο οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ δύναται ὁ υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφʼ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν ἐὰν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν πατέρα ποιοῦντα· ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: Apekrinato oun ho Iēsous kai elegen autois· Amēn amēn legō hymin, ou dynatai ho hyios poiein aphʼ heautou ouden ean mē ti blepē ton patera poiounta· ha gar an ekeinos poiē, tauta kai ho hyios homoiōs poiei.

paragraphs.text: For the Father loveth the Son, and showeth him all things that himself doeth: and greater works than these will he show him, that ye may marvel.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, καὶ μείζονα τούτων δείξει αὐτῷ ἔργα, ἵνα ὑμεῖς θαυμάζητε.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar patēr philei ton hyion kai panta deiknysin autō ha autos poiei, kai meizona toutōn deixei autō erga, hina hymeis thaumazēte.

paragraphs.text: For as the Father raiseth the dead and giveth them life, even so the Son also giveth life to whom he will.
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζῳοποιεῖ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζῳοποιεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar ho patēr egeirei tous nekrous kai zōopoiei, houtōs kai ho hyios hous thelei zōopoiei.

paragraphs.text: For neither doth the Father judge any man, but he hath given all judgment unto the Son;
paragraphs.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ υἱῷ,
paragraphs.translit: oude gar ho patēr krinei oudena, alla tēn krisin pasan dedōken tō hyiō,

paragraphs.text: that all may honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He that honoreth not the Son honoreth not the Father that sent him.
paragraphs.original: ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν πατέρα. ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hina pantes timōsi ton hyion kathōs timōsi ton patera. ho mē timōn ton hyion ou tima ton patera ton pempsanta auton.

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth him that sent me, hath eternal life, and cometh not into judgment, but hath passed out of death into life.
paragraphs.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν.
paragraphs.translit: Amēn amēn legō hymin hoti ho ton logon mou akouōn kai pisteuōn tō pempsanti me echei zōēn aiōnion, kai eis krisin ouk erchetai alla metabebēken ek tou thanatou eis tēn zōēn.

paragraphs.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour cometh, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live.
paragraphs.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ νεκροὶ ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀκούσαντες ζήσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Amēn amēn legō hymin hoti erchetai hōra kai nyn estin hote hoi nekroi akousousin tēs phōnēs tou hyiou tou theou kai hoi akousantes zēsousin.

paragraphs.text: For as the Father hath life in himself, even so gave he to the Son also to have life in himself:
paragraphs.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἔχει ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, οὕτως καὶ τῷ υἱῷ ἔδωκεν ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: hōsper gar ho patēr echei zōēn en heautō, houtōs kai tō hyiō edōken zōēn echein en heautō·

paragraphs.text: and he gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κρίσιν ποιεῖν, ὅτι υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: kai exousian edōken autō krisin poiein, hoti hyios anthrōpou estin.

paragraphs.text: Marvel not at this: for the hour cometh, in which all that are in the tombs shall hear his voice,
paragraphs.original: μὴ θαυμάζετε τοῦτο, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ἐν ᾗ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ
paragraphs.translit: mē thaumazete touto, hoti erchetai hōra en hē pantes hoi en tois mnēmeiois akousousin tēs phōnēs autou

paragraphs.text: and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐκπορεύσονται οἱ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ποιήσαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ δὲ τὰ φαῦλα πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekporeusontai hoi ta agatha poiēsantes eis anastasin zōēs, hoi de ta phaula praxantes eis anastasin kriseōs.

paragraphs.text: I can of myself do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is righteous; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.
paragraphs.original: Οὐ δύναμαι ἐγὼ ποιεῖν ἀπʼ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐδέν· καθὼς ἀκούω κρίνω, καὶ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ δικαία ἐστίν, ὅτι οὐ ζητῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με.
paragraphs.translit: Ou dynamai egō poiein apʼ emautou ouden· kathōs akouō krinō, kai hē krisis hē emē dikaia estin, hoti ou zētō to thelēma to emon alla to thelēma tou pempsantos me.

paragraphs.text: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
paragraphs.original: Ἐὰν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής·
paragraphs.translit: Ean egō martyrō peri emautou, hē martyria mou ouk estin alēthēs·

paragraphs.text: It is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμοῦ, καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἣν μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: allos estin ho martyrōn peri emou, kai oida hoti alēthēs estin hē martyria hēn martyrei peri emou.

paragraphs.text: Ye have sent unto John, and he hath borne witness unto the truth.
paragraphs.original: ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάννην, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκε τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·
paragraphs.translit: hymeis apestalkate pros Iōannēn, kai memartyrēke tē alētheia·

paragraphs.text: But the witness which I receive is not from man: howbeit I say these things, that ye may be saved.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε.
paragraphs.translit: egō de ou para anthrōpou tēn martyrian lambanō, alla tauta legō hina hymeis sōthēte.

paragraphs.text: He was the lamp that burneth and shineth; and ye were willing to rejoice for a season in his light.
paragraphs.original: ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: ekeinos ēn ho lychnos ho kaiomenos kai phainōn, hymeis de ēthelēsate agalliathēnai pros hōran en tō phōti autou·

paragraphs.text: But the witness which I have is greater than [that of] John; for the works which the Father hath given me to accomplish, the very works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔχω τὴν μαρτυρίαν μείζω τοῦ Ἰωάννου, τὰ γὰρ ἔργα ἃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ πατὴρ ἵνα τελειώσω αὐτά, αὐτὰ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιῶ, μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ὁ πατήρ με ἀπέσταλκεν,
paragraphs.translit: egō de echō tēn martyrian meizō tou Iōannou, ta gar erga ha dedōken moi ho patēr hina teleiōsō auta, auta ta erga ha poiō, martyrei peri emou hoti ho patēr me apestalken,

paragraphs.text: And the Father that sent me, he hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his form.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με πατὴρ ἐκεῖνος μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ ἐμοῦ. οὔτε φωνὴν αὐτοῦ πώποτε ἀκηκόατε οὔτε εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἑωράκατε,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho pempsas me patēr ekeinos memartyrēken peri emou. oute phōnēn autou pōpote akēkoate oute eidos autou heōrakate,

paragraphs.text: And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he sent, him ye believe not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ὑμῖν μένοντα, ὅτι ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος τούτῳ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ton logon autou ouk echete en hymin menonta, hoti hon apesteilen ekeinos toutō hymeis ou pisteuete.

paragraphs.text: Ye search the scriptures, because ye think that in them ye have eternal life; and these are they which bear witness of me;
paragraphs.original: Ἐραυνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς δοκεῖτε ἐν αὐταῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχειν· καὶ ἐκεῖναί εἰσιν αἱ μαρτυροῦσαι περὶ ἐμοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: Eraunate tas graphas, hoti hymeis dokeite en autais zōēn aiōnion echein· kai ekeinai eisin hai martyrousai peri emou·

paragraphs.text: and ye will not come to me, that ye may have life.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐ θέλετε ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχητε.
paragraphs.translit: kai ou thelete elthein pros me hina zōēn echēte.

paragraphs.text: I receive not glory from men.
paragraphs.original: δόξαν παρὰ ἀνθρώπων οὐ λαμβάνω,
paragraphs.translit: doxan para anthrōpōn ou lambanō,

paragraphs.text: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in yourselves.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἔγνωκα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: alla egnōka hymas hoti tēn agapēn tou theou ouk echete en heautois.

paragraphs.text: I am come in my Father`s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ ἐλήλυθα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ πατρός μου καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετέ με· ἐὰν ἄλλος ἔλθῃ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ, ἐκεῖνον λήμψεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: egō elēlytha en tō onomati tou patros mou kai ou lambanete me· ean allos elthē en tō onomati tō idiō, ekeinon lēmpsesthe.

paragraphs.text: How can ye believe, who receive glory one of another, and the glory that [cometh] from the only God ye seek not?
paragraphs.original: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι, δόξαν παρʼ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε;
paragraphs.translit: pōs dynasthe hymeis pisteusai, doxan parʼ allēlōn lambanontes, kai tēn doxan tēn para tou monou theou ou zēteite;

paragraphs.text: Think not that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, [even] Moses, on whom ye have set your hope.
paragraphs.original: μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα· ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε.
paragraphs.translit: mē dokeite hoti egō katēgorēsō hymōn pros ton patera· estin ho katēgorōn hymōn Mōysēs, eis hon hymeis ēlpikate.

paragraphs.text: For if ye believed Moses, ye would believe me; for he wrote of me.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί, περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar episteuete Mōysei, episteuete an emoi, peri gar emou ekeinos egrapsen.

paragraphs.text: But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασιν πιστεύσετε;
paragraphs.translit: ei de tois ekeinou grammasin ou pisteuete, pōs tois emois rhēmasin pisteusete;
